decisions.issues: Minor only. The top-left caption box hides the left half of João's belt and the lower jerkin, but the buckle, the iron key ring and the bucket all stay fully visible. The lighting is warm torchlight, with a barred gate and a wall sconce behind him. No neighbouring panels exist yet to compare against, so page 1 panels 1, 3 and 5 should be generated to match this lit cellar or state (the script's failing slit-window light). Otherwise clean: João's costume matches his sheet (quilted brown leather jerkin, cream shirt with rolled sleeves, wide belt with brass buckle, iron key ring, dark breeches, cream stockings, low buckled shoes); the low floor-level point of view shows the buckled shoe on the bottom stair with the keys and bucket; there is exactly one blank caption box with no tail, clear of the key action; there is no text or pseudo-text, noose, blood or anachronism; and both hands are sound.

v02 (the only candidate) gets a lot right. Nagoji matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, clean chin with light stubble, gold ear stud, long curly hair, ochre tunic, cream dhoti, bandaged wrists, ankle irons, barefoot, no brand showing. Joao matches his sheet: dense dark beard, brown jerkin, cream shirt, wide belt, keys, knee breeches, cream stockings, buckled shoes. The small musical notes are at his lips. There is exactly one blank balloon, upper centre, clear of both faces, and its tail points to Joao's mouth. Hands and anatomy are sound, with no text, noose or gore. It fails on four points. (1) Continuity: page 1.1 shows fifteen men in a row whose ankle irons share one long iron bar, and 2.2 shows Nagoji seated in that row. Here he sits alone on the floor, his ankle chain runs to a wall ring, and no other prisoner is in frame. (2) Two unscripted Portuguese guards stand in the background. The nearer one wears a brown leather jerkin, a wide brass-buckled belt and a dense beard, so he reads as a helmeted double of Joao. The book's guard rule is buff jerkin and no wide belt, so no guard reads as Joao, and neither 2.1 nor 2.2 shows guards. (3) The script beat is a tap on Nagoji's shoulder, but Joao's shoe toe presses his raised knee instead. (4) The rendering is noticeably cleaner and brighter than the gritty, damp stone in 1.1, 2.1 and 2.4.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition. Keep Joao on-sheet at left: dense dark beard, brown leather jerkin, cream shirt, wide belt with iron key ring, dark knee breeches, cream stockings, low buckled shoes. Keep the small musical notes at his humming lips. Keep Nagoji exactly as drawn, seated on the stone floor against the wall at right, looking up at Joao: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, gold ear stud, loose curly hair, torn ochre tunic, cream dhoti, bandaged wrists, bare feet. Keep the single blank speech balloon at upper centre with its tail to Joao's mouth. Fix four things. First, lift Joao's shoe so the toe taps the outer point of Nagoji's shoulder, not his knee: an easy, almost companionable nudge, with Joao's balance and the lifted leg drawn plausibly. Second, remove every guard and every other standing figure. No morions, no halberds; Joao is the only man on his feet. Third, restore the row of prisoners from page 1. Two or three other chained men sit on the floor along the same wall, partly cropped by the panel edge, heads bowed, in grey, brown and off-white rags, none in ochre. One long iron bar runs along the floor through all their ankle irons, Nagoji's included. There is no chain from Nagoji to a wall ring. Fourth, match the neighbouring panels' rendering: damp, slime-streaked stone and a wet floor, lit by a wall torch and the barred gate glowing at the end of the corridor behind. Keep the same warm-dark grade, not a clean or bright one.

decisions.issues: v03 is the only candidate and it gets almost everything right. Nagoji's face is on model: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin with light stubble, small gold ear stud, loose curly hair, torn ochre tunic, cream dhoti, barefoot with ankle irons. Duarte matches his sheet: gaunt, swept grey curls, plain black standing collar with no white tab, small cross on a thin chain, ink-stained fingers, torch in his right hand. Joao matches his sheet: full dark beard, brown jerkin over a cream shirt, wide belt, key ring, knee breeches, cream stockings, low buckled shoes. The staging works (Duarte leading in the foreground, Nagoji in the centre, Joao behind at left) in a low vaulted torchlit corridor with wet stone. It has exactly one blank caption box with no tail at upper left, clear of faces, and no text, noose, blood or anachronism. The one failure: Nagoji's bandaged wrists are locked in iron wrist manacles, and a long chain runs from them down to his ankle cuffs. The chapter 1 bible row allows only bandaged hands and wrists plus ankle irons; wrist manacles first appear in chapter 2. An earlier correction for this same panel (r7) already said to remove every wrist chain and wrist manacle, with no metal above the ankles. The irons also break continuity with 4.1, where his bandaged hands are free while the guards haul him up. The crossed wrists also bring his left forearm to the front of the body instead of keeping it turned from camera.
decisions.correction: Keep this exact composition, lighting and cast: Father Duarte leading in the right foreground with the torch in his right hand, ink-stained left hand, plain black standing collar and small cross; Nagoji in the centre with clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, gold ear stud, loose curly hair, torn ochre tunic and cream dhoti; Joao behind at left in brown jerkin, breeches, cream stockings, buckled shoes and key ring; the low vaulted torchlit stone corridor with wet flagstones; the single blank caption box at upper left. Change only Nagoji's restraints and arms. Remove the iron wrist manacles and the long chain from his wrists to his ankles completely, so there is no metal at all above his ankles. His hands hang separately at his sides, not crossed or joined. Both hands and wrists are wrapped only in cloth bandages, as in the previous panel where the guards haul him up. His left arm hangs on the far side of his body with the inner forearm turned toward his thigh, away from camera. His only irons are two iron ankle cuffs joined by a short chain that drags on the stone between his bare feet.

decisions.issues: v05, the only candidate, fails. (1) Wrong setting: a barred window with daylight shafts falling on the floor. The canonical chamber in 6.1, 6.2, 6.3 and 6.5 is a windowless, torchlit vaulted stone room with a wall torch, an iron brazier, a hanging rope ring and an arched wooden door, all under warm orange firelight. (2) Wrong speaker on the second balloon: both lines belong to João, but the right-hand balloon's tail points down-left at Nagoji's head, so the reader would give 'A pity. Fine animal.' to Nagoji. (3) Wrong framing: the script wants João in the background, but here he is large, at the left edge, and at the same depth as Nagoji or nearer, so the casual throwaway staging is lost. The character likenesses are good and can be kept. João matches his sheet: burly, curly-haired, bearded, brown leather jerkin, cream shirt, belt with key ring, pale stockings. Nagoji matches his sheet and the chapter 1 row: thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, loose curly hair, torn ochre tunic, cream dhoti, bandaged wrists roped to the stool, linked ankle irons, bare feet. The tongs action, the absence of painted text and the sound anatomy are also fine.
decisions.correction: Keep both likenesses and costumes exactly as drawn (Nagoji's rope-over-bandage wrist ties to the stool legs, linked ankle irons, bare feet, clean chin, gold stud; João's leather jerkin, cream shirt, belt, key ring, stockings, beard), but set the scene in the canonical interrogation chamber used on the rest of this page: a windowless vaulted stone room lit only by warm orange firelight from a wall torch in an iron bracket at left and an iron brazier at centre, with a hanging iron ring of ropes and an arched iron-studded wooden door at right. There must be NO window, NO bars and NO daylight shafts. Stage it as a wide horizontal panel matching the neighbouring frames. Nagoji sits bound on the stool in the left foreground, large and in three-quarter view. João stands small in the right background at the wooden tool table beside the door, head bowed, eyes on the iron tongs he is lifting, not looking at Nagoji. Reserve exactly two blank outlined speech balloons in the upper middle-right, clear of both faces. The first sits higher and further left, the second sits below and to the right of it, nearer João. BOTH tails must point visibly to João's mouth, and neither tail may point toward Nagoji.

decisions.issues: v03 (the only candidate listed; v01 and v02 are on the sheet but were not offered) gets Nagoji right: thick curled moustache, clean chin with light stubble, gold ear stud, loose curly hair, torn ochre sleeveless tunic. It has no painted text and the anatomy is sound. It fails on four counts. (1) It has ONE blank balloon, but 7.4 has three NAGOJI lines, so it needs three separate blank areas. (2) The setting is wrong. It shows cool grey stone with a barred window and daylight shafts. Panels 7.1 and 7.2 are the warm, torch-lit, windowless vaulted interrogation room (wall torch, brazier, orange light). The high window belongs only to the page 1 cellar. (3) He gazes up and off to frame right with a far-away look. That reads like the unfocused memory beat of 7.3, not 'present again, answering'. In 7.2 Duarte stands at frame left facing right, so Nagoji should look level toward frame left. (4) The one balloon's tail ends at the hair behind his jaw, not at his mouth, and his mouth is closed.
decisions.correction: Keep the tight head-and-shoulders close-up and Nagoji's exact likeness from the reference sheet: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin with only light captivity stubble, small gold ear stud on the visible ear, long loose curly black hair, torn ochre sleeveless tunic, no turban, no hands in frame, left arm out of view. Set it in the SAME torch-lit vaulted stone interrogation room as the neighbouring panels: warm orange torchlight and brazier glow raking his face from one side, dark rough stone blocks behind him softly out of focus, NO window, NO bars, NO daylight shafts, no cool grey light. Put his head in the right half of the panel, turned three-quarter toward frame LEFT, eyes level, sharp and focused on Duarte just off the left edge (present and defiant, not gazing upward or into the distance), lips slightly parted as he speaks. In the open space on the left and upper left, draw exactly THREE separate blank white outlined speech balloons, empty of any text. Stack them in reading order: the first and largest at top left, the second below it, the third smallest and lowest, closest to his face. Each balloon has its own short tail ending at his mouth. All three stay clear of his eyes, nose, moustache and mouth. No lettering or pseudo-text anywhere.

decisions.issues: Acceptable, with minor notes only. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch1 row: thick curled moustache, captivity stubble only on the chin, small gold ear stud, long curly hair, torn ochre sleeveless tunic, cream dhoti, bandaged hands and wrists, ankle irons, barefoot. His eyes are closed and he is slumped in the chained row with other prisoners, in a vaulted stone cellar lit by a wall sconce. That matches the script beat and the warm torchlight of 9.3. There is one blank outlined caption box at the top left, clear of faces and hands. There is no text, noose or anachronism, and the hands and feet are anatomically sound. The bandage stains are brown grime, the same hue as the dirt on the dhoti, not red blood. Nits: there is a faint thin pale line on his bare inner left forearm that could be misread as the scar that belongs to ch9 onward, though at print size it reads as a scratch or crease. The prisoners hang from individual wall rings, not the single ankle bar of page 1 panel 1, which is acceptable for this panel.
